summary: This is the abstract and reference list of Masanori Amano's chapter "The NAIRU, Potential Output, and the Kalman Filter: A Survey and Method of Estimation" in the book Money, Capital Formation and Economic Growth (Palgrave Macmillan, 2013). The abstract argues that the NAIRU and potential output matter more as central banks treat inflation as a key target, and that correctly forecasting the NAIRU lets policy authorities keep inflation stable. The page is otherwise mostly SpringerLink navigation and citation boilerplate; the note contains only the abstract and the bibliography, not the chapter's estimation method itself.
one_line: Amano's 2013 chapter surveying NAIRU and potential output estimation with the Kalman filter, framed around inflation targeting by central banks.
key_facts: The chapter is titled "The NAIRU, Potential Output, and the Kalman Filter: A Survey and Method of Estimation" and appears on pages 59–79 of the book Money, Capital Formation and Economic Growth.
The chapter's author is Masanori Amano of Chiba University, Japan.
The chapter was published in 2013 by Palgrave Macmillan, London, with DOI 10.1057/9781137281838_4.
The abstract says NAIRU stands for non-accelerating inflation rate of unemployment.
The abstract states that more central banks regard inflation as a main targeting variable in their policy operations, citing Bernanke and Mishkin (1997).
The abstract argues that if the central bank can correctly forecast the future course of the NAIRU and steer the economy to that position, the policy authority can obtain a stable rate of inflation.
The abstract adds that if the central bank can control the growth of money supply at least in the medium-term horizon, the inflation rate can be controlled at a low and stable level.
The listed keywords are Random Walk, Monetary Policy, Kalman Filter, Price Index and Potential Output.
The reference list includes Phillips (1958) on the relation between unemployment and the rate of change of money wages in the United Kingdom, 1861–1957.
The reference list includes Gordon, R.J. (1997) on the time-varying NAIRU and its implications for economic policy in the Journal of Economic Perspectives.
The reference list includes Staiger, Stock and Watson (1997a) on the NAIRU, unemployment, and monetary policy.
The reference list includes Kuttner (1994) on estimating potential output as a latent variable in the Journal of Business and Economic Statistics.
The reference list includes Friedman (1968) on the role of monetary policy in the American Economic Review.
The reference list includes Hamilton (1994) Time Series Analysis, published by Princeton University Press.
